Previously, viewing your history would unmount the underlying surface that keeps your session alive, which erased your session record and forced you back into the waiting room upon return. Now the history screen renders inside the same surface that holds your session, so the session stays mounted and intact while you browse. This affects anyone using the CLI to access chat history, and you'll notice the app no longer kicks you out or resets your session after viewing past conversations.

ai.title: Agent runtime preserves message history on mid-run errors
ai.summary: Agent runtime now mutates `initialAgentState` in place during `loopAgentSteps` instead of creating new objects, ensuring `messageHistory` propagates to SDK callers even if an error throws before return. SDK `run.ts` detects this progress via array identity comparison (`sessionState.mainAgentState.messageHistory !== initialMessageHistory`) to conditionally append the user prompt in `getCancelledSessionState`, preventing duplicate messages when the runtime already processed the input. Changes cover `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` and `sdk/src/run.ts`. The fix relies on shared object references and array identity checks rather than length comparisons to handle context pruning scenarios.

eli5.text: When an assistant is in the middle of working through a multi-step task and suddenly runs into an error, your conversation history used to get lost, meaning any progress made before the error would vanish. Now, that in-progress work is preserved so you don't lose what the assistant was already thinking or doing. If you were watching a session and saw it crash partway through, you'd now see the messages leading up to the error instead of a blank slate.
